'''''Acaena pinnatifida''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family ''[[Rosaceae]]''.<ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/8QH3 |title= Acaena pinnatifida Ruiz & Pav. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=January 26, 2025}}</ref> It is known by the common names '''Argentinian biddy-biddy''' and '''California sheepbur'''. It grows in California (United States), Argentina and Chile. The population from California is sometimes considered to be a distinct species or variety from the population in South America. 

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Acaena pinnatifida'' is known from California (in the United States), and in South America (Chile to Argentina).<ref name="POWO" /> In North America, the species grows on roadsides, sand dunes, rocky slopes and coastal grasslands.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Acaena pinnatifida - FNA |url=http://floranorthamerica.org/Acaena_pinnatifida |access-date=2025-01-05 |website=floranorthamerica.org}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Acaena pinnatifida'' was first formally named and described in 1798 by [[Hipólito Ruiz López]] and [[José Antonio Pavón Jiménez|José Antonio Pavón]] (Spanish botanists) in the ''Flora Peruviana, et Chilensis'' journal.<ref name=POWO>{{Cite POWO|id=720089-1|title=''Acaena pinnatifida'' Ruiz & Pav. | Plants of the World Online | Kew Science|access-date=5 January 2025}}</ref>

===Etymology===
In English, ''Acaena pinnatifida'' is commonly known as the ''Argentinian biddy-biddy'' and as the ''California sheepbur''.<ref name=NS />

===Varieties===
''Acaena pinnatifida'' is often discussed as consisting of distinct varieties. These include the following:

*''Acaeana pinnatifida'' var. ''californica'', which is endemic to coastal scrub areas and open rocky slopes in [[California]].  It is a perennial herb that flowers between March and May. It can be found at elevations ranging from {{cvt|50–400|m|ft}}. This variety has also been treated by some authorities as a distinct species (''Acaena californica'').<ref>{{Cite web |title=''Acaena californica'' |url=https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/eflora/eflora_display.php?tid=11685 |access-date=2025-01-05 |website=ucjeps.berkeley.edu}}</ref>
